clue.text: Where one's sister may be ahead

definitions.meaning: a sister is a senior hospital nurse in Britain, who works on a hospital ward

explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals 'sister' is the title of a senior nurse in charge of a ward, so read as two words the answer says where she is.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving forward means going ahead, and split in two the letters say a nurse is at work on the ward.

clue.text: Service no longer kept in reserve

definitions.meaning: a church service, as in the divine ... said daily
something kept in reserve is 'on ice', so once taken out it is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: 'On ice' is an idiom for held in reserve; its opposite, split as two words, spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily round of prayers in church is called the office, a form of religious service; split in two it means taken out of cold storage.

clue.text: No second course required after such bread?

definitions.text: No second course required after such bread?

parts.words: No second course required after such bread
parts.note: the bread's name, split into two words, would describe a complete dinner needing no further course

explanation.walkthrough: Brown bread made from unrefined flour has a name that, read as two words, means an entire dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread baked from unrefined flour including the bran; split, it is a complete dinner.

clue.text: Thoroughly straight person holding sway?

definitions.meaning: a measuring stick with a perfectly straight edge
a monarch or other sovereign who governs

explanation.definitionFit: A drawing instrument is perfectly straight-edged, and a sovereign is someone who governs.

clue.text: Precious stone brought Greek poetess endless anger

indicators.note: endless says the poetess's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Sappho was the lyric poet of ancient Lesbos
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A gem provoked fury in a poet of ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the O from SAPPHO, leaving SAPPH.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue gem of the corundum family, valued as a jewel.

clue.text: Delegate has a short time to collect information

indicators.note: to collect means the outer letters gather up the middle piece

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation of time
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A representative is given a brief window to gather facts.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information, as in 'get the gen'. 'to collect' puts it between A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sent to act on another's behalf is a representative, a noun sense of delegate.

clue.text: His topic? A curious nut-bearing tree

indicators.note: curious suggests something odd, so the letters are rearranged strangely

explanation.surface: Someone wonders at an odd subject of conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' rearranges the nine letters HISTOPICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Asian tree whose green kernels are eaten as snacks.

clue.text: Fireplace partially supporting ledge

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a hearth is a shelf that holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic and Scots word for a hearth, kept in 'inglenook'.

clue.text: Writer endlessly opposes getting state involved

indicators.note: involved means the second piece is wrapped up inside the first
endlessly strips both outside letters off the word for opposes

parts.note: resists means opposes or withstands
to say is to state

explanation.surface: An author keeps fighting and gets the government mixed up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips both outside letters of the opposing word, leaving ESIST, and 'involved' wraps those letters round the stating word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who composes short prose pieces on a subject is a kind of author.

clue.text: Departing relative's suspect behaviour

parts.note: going means leaving
a son is a family relative

explanation.surface: A family member leaving behaves dubiously.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady or improper conduct is described as goings-on.

clue.text: Eager to travel, potter about motors regularly

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the potter word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to footle about is to potter or dawdle aimlessly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of motors

explanation.surface: Someone tinkering with car engines longs to hit the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potter' looks like a maker of pots, but it is the verb meaning to dawdle; the British synonym needed is rare. 'about' wraps it round the alternate letters that 'regularly' takes, splitting it between L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of ties and keen to wander, like someone with nothing holding them back.

clue.text: Mathematician's symbols or functions, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver to go by how the word is spoken

parts.note: sines are trigonometric functions

explanation.surface: A maths student asks about notation or functions.
explanation.walkthrough: SINES and SIGNS sound the same; the plus and minus marks are what a mathematician writes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus, minus and similar marks are the basic notation of arithmetic.

clue.text: Badge one is never commissioned to wear

definitions.text: Badge one is never commissioned to wear

parts.words: Badge one is never commissioned to wear
parts.note: the V-shaped stripes on a sleeve mark a non-commissioned rank such as corporal or sergeant

explanation.walkthrough: The V-shaped sleeve stripes show non-commissioned ranks, so their wearer is an NCO, never a commissioned officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The inverted-V stripe worn on a sleeve to mark a corporal's or sergeant's rank.

clue.text: Attempt to adopt career identifying Gothic openwork

indicators.note: to adopt means taking another piece into the middle

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to career is to race along at speed

explanation.surface: Someone attempts a change of profession by studying medieval architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is a verb, to rush along, not a profession; 'to adopt' takes it inside the attempt word.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental stone ribs in the upper part of a Gothic window.

clue.text: Reportedly the sole beneficiary in the Faust legend?

definitions.text: Reportedly the sole beneficiary in the Faust legend?

parts.words: Reportedly the sole beneficiary in the Faust legend
parts.note: 'sole' said aloud is 'soul': the devil's agent is the one who gets Faust's soul in the pact

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' tells you to hear 'sole' as 'soul': the demon who wins Faust's soul gains from the bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: The demon to whom Faust sells his soul in the German legend.

clue.text: Game that's bound to go with whisky

parts.note: a bound is a hop or leap
Scotch is whisky from Scotland

explanation.surface: A pastime that is sure to go well with a dram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain', but it is the noun meaning a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground game of jumping through squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Lofty husband leaves virtuous fellow to entertain member

annotationWithheld.why: Lofty husband leaves virtuous fellow to entertain member (8): (H)OLY MAN gives OLYMAN, but no clue word gives the PI or I needed to make OLYMPIAN; 'member' gives MP, and the remaining I comes from no word
annotationWithheld.clue: Lofty husband leaves virtuous fellow to entertain member

clue.text: Sluggish girl teacher's thrown out without hesitation

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters are scattered into a new order
without here means minus, so the hesitation sound is subtracted from the pool

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter; the word is taken as it stands
er is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A lazy schoolgirl's teacher is expelled without a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' takes out ER; 'thrown out' rearranges the other letters of GIRL TEACHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking energy and drowsy, as someone dull and slow.

clue.text: Chair, possibly, a woman's used appropriately outside

indicators.note: outside means the phrase surrounds the woman

parts.note: a chair is used as intended when it is sat on
her stands for a woman; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman has handled a piece of furniture properly.
explanation.walkthrough: A chair is used appropriately when SAT ON; 'outside' puts it round HER. Sheraton is a style of English furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An English furniture style of the late 1700s, named after its designer, so a seat may be one.

clue.text: Ungenerous response to an offer for one's thoughts

definitions.text: Ungenerous response to an offer for one's thoughts

parts.words: Ungenerous response to an offer for one's thoughts
parts.note: the saying 'a penny for your thoughts' offers a coin; replying that they are worth half as much is mean

explanation.walkthrough: 'A penny for your thoughts' is the offer; answering that they are worth only half that is ungenerous. The old halfpenny was a British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount, literally as much as an old half-penny coin would buy.

clue.text: Live with carrier below shop

indicators.note: below says in this down answer one word sits under the other

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a tray carries things

explanation.surface: Someone lives above the store with a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is a verb, British slang for informing on someone, not a store.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on someone to the authorities is to give them away.

clue.text: Extremely rude set of songs to salvage for further use

indicators.note: extremely means taking the first and last letters of rude

parts.note: a song cycle is a set of songs

explanation.surface: A coarse collection of tunes is rescued to be used again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprocess waste so its material can be used again.

clue.text: Tolstoy was one to consider

definitions.meaning: Leo Tolstoy held a noble title in Russia
to take into account or reckon

explanation.definitionFit: The Russian novelist was a nobleman of that rank, and to reckon is to take into account.

clue.text: Sly person's wife's lost artist's support

indicators.note: lost means the wife abbreviation is dropped from the word

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person; the 's is 'has'
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A crafty man has lost his wife, and a painter's prop besides.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden stand that holds a painter's canvas.

clue.text: Pacify volunteers put back in position

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the word for position

parts.note: a place is a position

indicators.note: put back says these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers are returned to their posts to calm them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's reserve of volunteer soldiers. 'put back' turns its abbreviation into AT, and 'in' sets that inside the position word.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe or appease someone who is angry.

clue.text: Venue for contests a long time back

indicators.note: back says the two pieces together are read in reverse

parts.note: an is the form of the article a
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A place for competition existed long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns both pieces round together as one run, giving the stadium word; turning only the long time would not work.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or enclosed space where sporting contests take place.

clue.text: Pin one's faith on commercial credit

definitions.meaning: to rely on or believe in
goods supplied on ... are supplied on credit

explanation.definitionFit: To believe in is to rely on, and in business supplying goods 'on trust' means on deferred payment.

clue.text: One feeds on carrion? Even crags may provide it

indicators.note: may provide hints the letters, rearranged, can be made into the answer

explanation.surface: A vulture-like creature finds its food among the level rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may provide' rearranges the nine letters of EVEN CRAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature that lives on dead flesh, such as a vulture or hyena.

clue.text: It's hard, containing a possible source of allergy

definitions.text: It's hard, containing a possible source of allergy

parts.words: It's hard, containing a possible source of allergy
parts.note: a hard outer case around a kernel, a common trigger of allergic reactions

explanation.walkthrough: Peanuts and tree nuts are common allergens, and the hard case around them is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard woody casing around a kernel.

clue.text: Notedly attractive girl touring clubs

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the name surrounds the letter

parts.note: Cathy is a girl's name
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A young woman visits nightspots and looks fetching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' means in musical notes: a catchy tune is easy to remember.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that appeals and sticks in the memory.
